name: Zalmunna
title: Midianite king
summary: Zalmunna was one of the two kings of Midian who were defeated by Gideon. Together with Zebah, he led a large Midianite army that plundered and oppressed Israel. Gideon pursued and captured both kings, executing them in revenge for the killing of his brothers at Tabor.

keyEvents.title: Midianite oppression of Israel
keyEvents.description: Zalmunna and Zebah were kings over the Midianites who for years had plundered and oppressed Israel, destroying their crops and livestock.

keyEvents.title: Gideon's victory over the Midianites
keyEvents.description: Gideon defeated the large Midianite army with only 300 men, and Zalmunna and Zebah fled with the rest of their forces.

keyEvents.title: Gideon pursues Zalmunna and Zebah
keyEvents.description: Gideon and his 300 men pursued Zebah and Zalmunna across the Jordan, exhausted but steadfast. The people of Sukkoth and Peniel refused to give them food.

keyEvents.title: The Capture of Zebah and Zalmunna
keyEvents.description: Gideon surprised the Midianite camp at Karkor and captured Zebah and Zalmunna. Their entire army of about 15,000 men was scattered.

keyEvents.title: The Revelation About the Brothers at Tabor
keyEvents.description: Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna about the men they had killed at Tabor. They admitted that these men resembled Gideon's brothers and confirmed that they had killed them.

keyEvents.title: The Execution of Zebah and Zalmunna
keyEvents.description: Gideon ordered his firstborn son Jether to kill the kings, but he was too young and afraid. Zebah and Zalmunna asked Gideon to do it himself, so Gideon killed them and took the crescent ornaments from the camels' necks.
